title: Working Scientifically
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Working Scientifically Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_code: AC9S3I01, AC9S3I02, AC9S3I03, AC9S3I04, AC9S3I05, AC9S3I06
standard_text: Pose questions and make predictions; plan and conduct safe, fair investigations; observe and measure with simple equipment; record data in tables and simple graphs; identify patterns; and share findings (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Year 3 science inquiry content descriptions).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on working scientifically: questions and predictions, fair and safe tests, measuring with a ruler and thermometer, tally tables and graphs, and sharing results. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A fair test changes one thing; measuring with tools beats guessing.
body_html:
How to think about it

Scientists find out by asking questions and testing them fairly.

  • Ask a question you can test and make a prediction.
  • Change one thing, keep everything else the same, and stay safe.
  • Measure with tools, record in a table or tally, and share what you found, even if it surprised you.
Example

Ball on grass 30 cm, concrete 60 cm. Highest bounce?

compare the numbers

Answer: concrete

Example

Tally: ||||/ ||. How many?

a crossed group is 5

5 + 2

Answer: 7

Common mistakes

  • Changing more than one thing at a time.
  • Guessing instead of measuring.
  • Changing results so they match the prediction.

faq.a: A fair test changes only one thing and keeps everything else the same.
Each stroke is one. The fifth stroke crosses the first four, so each crossed group is 5.
Science is about finding out what really happens. Surprising results help us learn.

items.q: Is this an observation or an inference (an explanation)? “The lamp glowed brighter with two batteries.”
c: a prediction made before the test
items.e: An observation is what you saw or measured; an inference explains it.

items.q: What is a mean?
c: the result in the middle of the table
the total of the results divided by how many results there are
items.e: An average.

items.q: Which of these questions can be answered by a fair test?
c: Does salt water freeze faster than tap water?
Which day of the week is the best?
Is science more fun than art?
items.e: A testable question changes one thing and measures another.

items.q: Kai's results do not match his prediction. What should he do?

items.e: Honest results are part of science.

items.q: Mia drops a ball onto grass, concrete and sand from 1 m. Bounce heights: 30 cm, 60 cm, 5 cm. Which surface gave the highest bounce?

items.q: Ruby says her seeds grew because she sang to them. How could she test this fairly?
